title: Adding hydrodynamics and random actuation made simulated gaits match living ones

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Adding hydrodynamics and random actuation made simulated gaits match living ones

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Designs first evolved on simulated land had bounding gaits that did not transfer to living organisms; adding first-order hydrodynamics and randomized phase offsets produced designs whose behaviour better matched the living systems, in contact with the ground for 93.3% of evaluation versus 52.7% on the first pass.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Materials and Methods › Evolutionary Design.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The behavior of designs generated on the second pass better matched the behavior of the actual living systems: on average, designs were in contact with the ground plane for 93.3% of their evaluation period, compared to just 52.7% on the first pass (SI Appendix, section S6).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Kriegman S, Blackiston D, Levin M, Bongard J, “A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms”, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (2020), doi:10.1073/pnas.1910837117; section “Materials and Methods › Evolutionary Design.”. Scope: Soft-body voxel simulations of Xenopus reconfigurable organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2020-xenobots-10: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.86

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The comparison, metric, and computational systems are explicit. Reimplementation can test the numerical result now, although the bundled modifications weaken separate causal attribution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reproduce first- and second-pass simulations and compute ground-contact fraction and gait descriptors, testing whether hydrodynamics plus randomized phase offsets account for the reported 52.7% to 93.3% change.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Exact values may depend on implementation and seeds.

The two simulator changes are bundled, limiting attribution to either one separately.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The quantitative content is a pair of ground-contact fractions from two specified simulation passes, and the code for those passes is public. Recomputing contact time confirms or refutes the 93.3 versus 52.7 percent contrast with a standard geometric measurement. The link to living gaits is the reason the second pass was defined, and it is checked by whether that pass stays on the substrate as the paper's living builds do.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Re-evaluate pass-1 and pass-2 designs in the deposited simulator and compute the fraction of time steps with ground contact; the numerical claim holds if pass 2 is near 93.3 percent and pass 1 near 52.7 percent under the published evaluation window.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Living ground-contact was not deposited as a paired percentage, so the match to organisms is carried by the simulation contrast.

Matching the published percentages requires the same evaluation window and random seeds described in the supplement.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: Designs evolved for locomotion on simulated land with evolvable (finely tuned) actuation phases spend a large fraction of their evaluation airborne, whereas designs evolved with first-order hydrodynamics (reduced gravity plus surface drag) and random clade-fixed phase offsets stay in contact with the ground almost all the time, as living deciliated organisms do (93.3% vs 52.7% ground contact in the paper).

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Tier A (published outputs or original simulator): mean ground-contact fraction of second-pass designs within 5 percentage points of 93.3% and of first-pass designs within 5 points of 52.7%, and second minus first >= 20 points. Tier B (simplified re-implementation, numbers not expected to match): mean contact fraction of second-pass champions >= 85% and second minus first >= 20 percentage points, with a permutation test p < 0.05 over trials. Contact at a time step = lowest node within 0.05 voxel lengths of the ground plane; fraction taken over the evaluation period.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: refutes if second-pass contact fraction <= first-pass + 5 points (no improvement), or (Tier A) if either published mean differs from the paper's figure by > 15 points. Other outcomes are 'mixed'. If neither published outputs nor a runnable simulator is available, verdict inconclusive (data-unavailable).
